authority.legacy_boundary: Existing D1/R2 Worker remains an unchanged baseline and read-only export source; the new service layer performs no D1/R2 writes

blockers_repaired: Composite tenant foreign keys bind validations, artifacts, exports, and evidence packages
private.finalize_validation requires approved review state plus service-verified original, manifest, and PDF Storage receipts

Dependency-safe cascades preserve append-only client semantics while permitting complete tenant teardown

controlled_intake: database intake/outbox atomic wiring remains a production integration gap

verification.evidence: 17 site assertions; syntax and generated Worker types current
1 repeatable behavioral pgTAP suite, 23 assertions per run
no security or performance issues at warn level

security_assertions: RLS enabled on every new public table with explicit least-privilege grants and policies
no public bucket or browser service-role secret
evidence, extraction, correction, obligation, and delivery business relations use composite tenant foreign keys
all new definer functions are private, have empty search_path, check auth.uid-bound membership, revoke PUBLIC/anon, and grant authenticated explicitly
finalization requires a service-written Storage HEAD and SHA-256 verification receipt; bytes remain operated through the Storage API
delivery rows and source hashes are created only by an auth.uid-bound RPC from validated evidence packages, and verified status requires a matching service-role destination digest
a service receipt explicitly recording no destination digest results in delivered_unverified, never verified
an exact attempt-key replay returns its immutable receipt before connector and terminal guards, while changed replay inputs conflict
destination behavior is locally simulated and no external network or real destination was exercised

payload_digest.canonicalization: recursively sort object keys, preserve array order, UTF-8 encode JSON.stringify output, and exclude the top-level payload_digest member

residual_unknowns: No production provider or customer corpus was used, so OCR accuracy and the 300-document benchmark remain unproven

Storage object existence is attested by a service receipt and still cannot be proven transactionally by Postgres alone; production orchestration must perform Storage HEAD and SHA-256 verification before writing that receipt
